messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: PrivateConnect peerlink (peer-azb) error rate spike > 15% for customer-corp in eu-central-1b. autodetect: increased TCP RSTs, DNS timeouts. Escalation paging sent to oncall team.

oncall-maya: got it. I'll take lead. Paging in #eng-oncall and adding network-sam. triage windows: 04:17 UTC.

incident-bot: Pager delivered to oncall-maya at 04:17:10 UTC. Incident ID: INC-2026-273912.

support-jess: customer-corp reports their webhook traffic to our hosted endpoint is returning 504s and DNS lookups failing intermittently since ~04:10 UTC. Support ticket 8942 opened. Customer impact: partial outage to one AZ.

network-sam: jumping in — pulling BGP + DNS telemetry now. @oncall-maya can you confirm which peerlink? peer-azb (vpc-peering-id: pcx-0b1234) per alert.

oncall-maya: confirmed. please paste first-pass commands you want.

network-sam: running quick checks:
```
# bgp summary (peer-azb)
Neighbor        AS    State    Prefixes    LastChange
10.10.11.1     64512  flapping   1200       00:00:12
```
looks noisy. also seeing route withdrawal bursts from eu-central-1b -> eu-central-1a every ~30s.

se-ryan: adding dataplane metrics:
- edge-proxy (eu-central-1b) 5xx rate up 18%
- dns-resolver (azb) median latency 420ms (norm 18ms)
- prefix cache miss rate increased 9x

network-sam: hypothesis: AZ internal fabric congestion causing BGP session jitter + DNS resolver timeouts. might be local AS path oscillation causing traffic to bounce across AZs.

cloud-provider-bot: GCP internal notice: "We are investigating network fabric anomalies impacting eu-central-1b inter-AZ routing. Engineers engaged. Reference INC-GCP-4372". Link: https://status.gcp.example/INC-GCP-4372

oncall-maya: thanks. immediate mitigation strategy: 1) avoid eu-central-1b for affected customer traffic by shifting route preference; 2) failover customer traffic to privateconnect via eu-central-1a; 3) maintain watch and coordinate with provider. Who can run the route preference change?

network-sam: I can. Plan: advertise a more-specific (/32 on the customer VIP) with local-pref to prefer our eu-central-1a path from the edge routers, plus temporarily disable ECMP on that peer for the customer. Doing a quick dry-run on staging router.

se-ryan: suggest also bump TTL on DNS responses and enable resolver fallback to resolver-b (eu-central-1a) to reduce DNS timeouts. I can flip resolver fallback routing.

oncall-maya: please go ahead. coordinate carefully, small steps. inform customer after first change.

network-sam: applying change to edge-router-03 (controlled rollout):
```
configure router edge-router-03
  neighbor 10.10.11.1 route-map PREFER_EUCA out
  route-map PREFER_EUCA permit 10
    set local-preference 200
    match ip address prefix-list CUSTOMER-CORP-VIP
commit
```
applying to 1/3 edge routers now.

(2m) network-sam: applied to edge-router-03, no immediate error spike. applying to edge-router-01 -> 2/3.

(4m) network-sam: applied to all 3 routers. monitoring. BGP flaps dropping from ~30s to >600s between updates.

support-jess: customer-corp updated: "We're seeing dropped webhooks but it's improving since 04:23". they appreciate the update.

se-ryan: resolver fallback flip done: dns-resolver cluster now favors eu-central-1a nodes for customer-corp queries. Median latency back to 28ms for the customer namespace.

incident-bot: automated checks: edge-proxy 5xx rate reduced to 2.1% (target <3%). DNS median latency 30ms. Continued monitoring.

network-sam: cloud-provider status just updated: "Mitigation in progress; fabric congestion reduced". Still seeing some residual route withdrawal noise but frequency down.

sre-aria: good work. let's prepare for handoff to the second shift. @oncall-maya please include short summary and remaining actions.

oncall-maya: Handoff summary for 05:00 UTC shift:
- Root cause (probable): GCP eu-central-1b internal fabric congestion causing BGP session jitter and DNS resolver timeouts -> traffic oscillation and increased 5xx for customer-corp over PrivateConnect.
- Mitigation performed: temporary local-pref advertisement to prefer eu-central-1a + disabled ECMP for customer VIP + DNS resolver fallback to eu-central-1a.
- Current state: customer connectivity restored; edge 5xx back to baseline; BGP flaps reduced but not zero.
- Follow-ups: monitor for 1h, coordinate with cloud-provider for final root cause, schedule postmortem, consider more durable routing policy (avoid single-AZ path for critical peers).

network-sam: I'm going to request a soft reset of the affected BGP neighbor from the provider side to clear flapping state. raising ticket to provider with requested time window: ASAP.

cloud-provider-bot: Ticket INC-GCP-4372 updated: provider scheduled soft-reset for peer-azb at 05:12 UTC. Engineers will perform tests post-reset and share logs.

support-jess: notified customer-corp of the mitigation and that we're monitoring. they confirmed webhook delivery resumed. going to keep the ticket open for postmortem.

sre-aria: assign postmortem: SRE + Network + Provider liaisons. Need timeline + config diffs + BGP dumps + resolver traces. I'll create a postmortem doc and invite ops + engineering leads.

oncall-maya: handing off to @sre-aria at 05:00 UTC. I'm available on-call if it re-escalates.

sre-aria: taking over. Action items for next shift:
- validate provider post-reset logs and confirm stable BGP for 6 hours
- run traceroutes from customer vantage and internal probes to ensure no path stretch (>50ms)
- produce RCA draft within 24 hours

network-sam: uploading bgp-dumps and dns-traces to incident storage: gs://incidents/2739123456/ (links pasted in case notes).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-273912 transitioned to monitoring at 04:31:22 UTC. Severity downgraded to SEV3.

sre-aria: closing thread for active mitigation. will update when postmortem drafted. thanks team. :thumbsup:
